title: Common strata carrying finite-type module trivializations
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $R$ a commutative ring, and choose either the small étale sites of all schemes or their small pro-étale sites [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaf $\underline R$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and the corresponding inverse-image restrictions [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image, def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Let $F_1,\ldots,F_r$ be a finite family of such module sheaves on $X$. Suppose for each $j$ there is an open covering of $X$ on each member $U$ of which a finite stratification [def-constructible-stratification] by constructible [def-weil-constructible-subset] locally closed subschemes makes $F_j$ locally constant of finite type; this means locally isomorphic to the constant sheaf of a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-locally-constant-module-sheaf]. Then there is one open covering on each member $U$ of which there is a finite stratification $i_\lambda:T_\lambda\to U$ making all $F_j$ locally constant of finite type; this covering may be taken to consist of all intersections $U=U_1\cap\cdots\cap U_r$ with each $U_j$ a member of the $j$-th input covering. More precisely, after restricting the input stratification of each $U_j$ to $U$, one may take $T_\lambda$ to be the nonempty finite fibre products over $U$ of one stratum from each input stratification [def-pc-fibre-product]. These are constructible locally closed subschemes with pairwise disjoint images covering $U$ and have the actual projection morphisms $h_{\lambda,j}$ to the input strata. For every chosen local trivialization of an input restriction with model $M$, its covering pulls back to a covering of $T_\lambda$ on which $i_\lambda^*F_j$ is the constant module sheaf with the same model $M$. The identification uses the canonical constant-ring inverse-image isomorphism, adjoint to constant sections, and is compatible with the inverse-image composition isomorphism for $i_\lambda$ and $h_{\lambda,j}$. No finiteness of the underlying set of $R$ or Noetherian hypothesis on $R$ is assumed. The empty family admits the one-stratum stratification $U=X$.

source.place: Tag 093R, lemma-pullback-locally-constant (including modules over a fixed ring); the finite fibre-product refinement and constant-section compatibility expand the common-strata argument in the retained finite-reductions proof Step 6.

proof.text: For $r=0$, use the single open $X$ and its identity stratum. Its image is constructible: $X$ and $\varnothing$ are retrocompact opens, since their intersections with a quasi-compact open are that open and the empty set. This is a stratification by the definition, even when $X$ is empty. For $r>0$, take all intersections $U=U_1\cap\cdots\cap U_r$ of members of the given open coverings. They are open and cover $X$: for each $x\in X$, choose one $U_j$ containing $x$ for each of the finitely many $j$. Empty intersections can be retained or discarded. Fix such a $U$ for the remaining steps.

source.place: Tags 005G (definition-constructible), 005H (lemma-constructible); empty-family case and finite intersections of open coverings

proof.text: Write $S_{j,a}\to U_j$ for the $j$-th input stratification. Pull it back along $U\to U_j$ using [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification]. This gives a finite stratification $S'_{j,a}=U\times_{U_j}S_{j,a}\to U$ with images the inverse images of the original stratum images. Those images are constructible by [lem-pur-scheme-constructible-preimage], since $U\to U_j$ is a scheme morphism; no quasi-compactness assumption on this open is needed. Keep the projection $S'_{j,a}\to S_{j,a}$ from [def-pc-fibre-product]. Thus all input partitions now have the same base $U$ and actual morphisms to their original strata.

source.place: Tag 054I, lemma-inverse-image-constructible; scheme-theoretic base change of a stratification

proof.text: Construct the common partition by induction on the number $m$ of input partitions already used. At $m=1$ use $S'_{1,a}\to U$. Given an immersion $p:P\to U$ in the current finite partition, pull the $(m+1)$-st stratification back to $P$ by [lemma-constructible-pullback-stratification]. Its strata are $Q_a=P\times_U S'_{m+1,a}\to P$; they form a finite disjoint covering of $P$ with images $p^{-1}(|S'_{m+1,a}|)$. Their composites to $U$ are immersions by clause (e) of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence]. An immersion is injective on underlying points: factor it as closed followed by open, each a homeomorphism onto its image [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-open-immersion]. Consequently the composite image is exactly $|P|\cap|S'_{m+1,a}|$. Running over all $P$ therefore gives a disjoint covering of $U$. It is finite because it is indexed by a finite union of finite sets. This proves the inductive assertion with the actual iterated fibre products, rather than replacing an image containment by a scheme factorization.

source.place: Tag 02V0, lemma-composition-immersion; Tags 01IO and 01HE (immersions); finite iteration of the pullback-stratification statement

proof.text: At the end of this induction every image is $\bigcap_{j=1}^r|S'_{j,a_j}|$. These images are constructible by finite-intersection closure in [def-weil-constructible-subset]. Each map is an immersion and hence gives a locally closed scheme stratum by [def-constructible-stratification]. Remove empty products. The universal property of [def-pc-fibre-product] identifies each iterated product with the chosen finite fibre product $T_\lambda$ and supplies projections to every factor. Composing with $S'_{j,a_j}\to S_{j,a_j}$ gives $h_{\lambda,j}:T_\lambda\to S_{j,a_j}$, and the composite to $X$ equals $T_\lambda\xrightarrow{i_\lambda}U\to X$ by the defining projection equations. Thus the asserted common stratification and all its projection morphisms have been constructed.

source.place: Tag 005H, lemma-constructible; fibre-product universal property, Tags 01JP and 001V

proof.text: For the coefficient identifications, use the prescribed sheafification and module adjunctions directly. Base change on either scheme site preserves finite limits and hence the terminal object; AsSmall transport preserves this property. The composite of constant sheafification with ring inverse image and target constant sheafification are left adjoint to the same terminal evaluation functor. Uniqueness of left adjoints gives an isomorphism, and its adjunct is rho because both fix constant scalars. For a module M, construct the normalized constant comparison by sheafifying the presheaf map sending m to the constant section m after base change, checking linearity using the scalar equation. Evaluation at a terminal object classifies maps from a constant module presheaf. Thus precomposition by the specified module comparison is bijective on maps into every module sheaf: the two module sheafification adjunctions and the inverse-image adjunction identify it with restriction of scalars along the same constant-section ring equation. The coyoneda criterion makes this comparison invertible, for arbitrary M and R. These are the completed Lean proofs of adicStratificationRingMap_isIso, adicStratificationConstantMap_existsUnique and adicStratificationConstantMap_isIso; no geometric algebraic-structure lift is needed for these canonical module pullbacks.

source.place: Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi (fixed-ring modules); Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; proetale.tex Tag 09A5, section-morphism

proof.text: For either choice of site, pulling back a chosen trivializing covering $\{V_b\to S\}$ along a morphism $h:T\to S$ gives a covering $\{T\times_SV_b\to T\}$. For the etale site use [lem-weil-pbc-etale-covering-base-change]. For the pro-etale site the arrows remain weakly etale by [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], and the covering is fpqc by [lem-galois-fpqc-covering-base-change]; this is precisely a covering in [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $h_b:T\times_SV_b\to V_b$ for the projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-localize-ringed-site-morphism], applied to the morphism of sites of $h$ (base-change functor $u(V)=T\times_SV$, constant coefficient rings and the ring map of step 5), restriction to $V_b$ followed by the localized inverse image is canonically isomorphic to inverse image followed by restriction to $u(V_b)=T\times_SV_b$: $(h^*G)|_{T\times_SV_b}\cong h_b^*(G|_{V_b})$ as module sheaves on the localized site. If the original restriction on $V_b$ is $\underline{M_b}$, applying the localized inverse image to that isomorphism identifies its pullback with $\underline{M_b}$ on $T\times_SV_b$ by [lem-sfb-geometric-inverse-image-constant-module]. The model is the same $R$-module $M_b$, not its underlying finite set and not a finite presentation. Its given finite generating list remains unchanged.

source.place: Tag 093R, lemma-pullback-locally-constant, omitted proof expanded using constant-module inverse image and covering base change (Tags 02GO, 01S1, 094U, 022D)

proof.text: Specify direct-image pasting on sections by restriction along the finite-fibre-product pasting isomorphism. The scalar maps agree by checking constant scalars under the ring sheafification adjunction. Mathlib pushforwardComp followed by pushforwardCongr₂ supplies this isomorphism, uniquely characterized by its section maps (adicStratificationPushforwardComp_existsUnique). Its adjunction mate is the specified inverse-image composition isomorphism. The conjugate adjunction unit identity computes the adjunct of composition through that mate. Applying the constant-module comparisons twice sends each generator m to m on the iterated fibre product. Naturality of the constant-module sheafification unit identifies this with the direct constant section under pasting. The uniqueness proved in step 5 therefore gives adicStratificationConstantMap_comp. This completes the constant-section composition compatibility in Lean.

source.place: Tag 0H7J, example-constant-sheaf; Tag 00YV, proposition-functoriality-algebraic-structures-topoi; comparison on constant coproduct inclusions

proof.text: Apply steps 5-7 to each projection $h_{\lambda,j}:T_\lambda\to S_{j,a_j}$ from step 4 and to every chosen covering and trivialization of $F_j|_{S_{j,a_j}}$. The equation between composites to $X$ in step 4 and the composition comparison of step 7 identify its pulled-back restriction with $i_\lambda^*(F_j|_U)$. Step 6 gives exactly the requested pulled-back covering and its unchanged finitely generated module model. Such a covering exists for each $j$ by hypothesis, so [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-locally-constant-module-sheaf] makes every $i_\lambda^*F_j$ locally constant of finite type: over any further site object pull these coverings back again to obtain its covering-sieve formulation. The same argument applies first to the open restriction $S'_{j,a_j}\to S_{j,a_j}$ of step 2. Together with the open covering of step 1 and the finite constructible stratification of steps 3-4, this proves every clause. Empty schemes and empty products cause no additional local requirement. Neither the construction nor the constant-module comparison required a finite underlying set for $R$ or a Noetherian ring.
